data.content_ref: inline:The target's claim states that the constant-difference shortcut 'will wrongly produce 33.' However, the shortcut as defined, x ≡ (r1−m1) ≡ (r2−m2) (mod lcm), is incoherent when the differences are unequal: (3−5)=−2 and (4−7)=−3 have no single common residue. The target cannot identify what concrete arithmetic steps yield 33 from this shortcut, since applying x ≡ −2 (mod 35) gives 33 but that is just one of the two differences, not a common residue; applying x ≡ −3 (mod 35) gives 32. The target concedes that 33 = 18−(−15) is merely a 'coincidental near-miss,' which contradicts the assertion that 33 is the output of the defined shortcut. The covering principle being sought—a general account of why the shortcut fails—requires a deterministic connection between the shortcut and its alleged output, not an unexplained coincidence.
